title: Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO of Nvidia, stock up 30%
snippet: Nvidia has announced that disgraced CEO Jensen Huang has been reinstated to the role, effective immediately. The company’s share price jumped more than 30% in response, with the rest of the market also making significant gains. It said that the board voted unanimously in favor of reinstatement despite its recent statement that it had no intention of doing so … more…
fullText:
Nvidia has announced that disgraced CEO Jensen Huang has been reinstated to the role, effective immediately. The company’s share price jumped more than 30% in response, with the rest of the market also making significant gains.

It said that the board voted unanimously in favor of reinstatement despite its recent statement that it had no intention of doing so …

The ‘resignation’

Huang’s affair with a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy became the main headline news in the tech press after coming to light at the end of last month. The New York Times broke the story on October 29, citing it then as “a close relationship.” Nvidia initially denied that the relationship was anything out of the ordinary.

That changed on November 8 when Huang publicly admitted to the affair. Nvidia’s shares dropped 5%, and the company’s board of directors opened an independent investigation. Further details emerged over the following days. Things got even worse when the same paper reported that Huang had also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him. 

That led to Huang being fired resigning on November 12. 

Calls for reinstatement

	

Despite putting the company at enormous risk and initially lying to its board of directors, there were calls in some quarters for Huang to be reinstated. He responded by saying that he would be “honored” to return if asked to do so.

The board of directors, however, said that it had no intention of inviting him back.

Nvidia’s chair Harvey Jones said: “The board does not intend to reinstate him.”

The reinstatement

That changed today, with the company making the announcement in a press release.

Nvidia today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.” 

As previously announced, in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, the Board formed a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate, and the committee retained independent counsel to assist it in that investigation. The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.

Stock up 30%+

title: 1Password said hackers broke into its internal systems, but customer passwords are safe
snippet: The password manager maker said an attacker gained access to an employee's corporate account and took some information about customers.
fullText:
Image Credits:1Password	

	

						

10:49 AM PST · November 25, 2026

											

			

Password manager maker 1Password has confirmed that some customer information was taken in a recent intrusion into its internal systems, but that customer password vaults and other secrets were not accessed.

The Toronto-based tech company said in a blog post published Wednesday that it detected an intrusion on November 19, in which an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate account with GitHub, which the company uses to share and store its source code.

The attacker used that employee’s access to push malicious code to the company’s internal servers, which allowed the hacker to download some data about 1Password customers, including their names and the email address that they use for logging into their account. The company said that the attacker also took details about when a 1Password account was created and when a user last logged in.

1Password said that customer vaults, which store their passwords, were “at no point” available to the attacker. The company also said that it doesn’t have access to customer account passwords or their secret keys, which are used to scramble their passwords so that 1Password cannot see them.

In addition, the company said that its apps and extensions are unaffected by the incident.

It’s unclear how the attacker gained access to the employee’s corporate account, and a spokesperson for 1Password did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s questions about the incident. 

1Password did not say whether it had notified customers whose information was taken in the breach, or how many customers had information taken. We’ve also asked if the company has received any communication or demands from the hackers. We’ll update if we hear back from 1Password.

The company touts millions of customers and more than 200,000 businesses who use its password manager products to store their passwords, credentials, payment card information, and more. Security experts have long recommended password managers as a better way of generating stronger credentials and keeping track of online accounts.

title: ‘Galaxy Watch 10’ won’t launch in 2027 as Samsung tries to slow RAMageddon losses
snippet: According to a new report, Samsung’s next “Galaxy Watch 10” won’t be releasing in 2027 with the company moving to a bi-yearly release schedule for its smartwatches. more…
fullText:
According to a new report, Samsung’s next “Galaxy Watch 10” won’t be releasing in 2027 with the company moving to a bi-yearly release schedule for its smartwatches.

ETNews reports that Samsung will not have a new Galaxy Watch model releasing in 2027, a series that would have likely been called “Galaxy Watch 10.” The reason, the report suggests, is that Samsung is “undertaking a structural overhaul to strengthen profitability” (translated) following two quarters in a row of losses in its mobile division. 

Samsung has released a new Galaxy Watch every year since 2018, with 2021’s Galaxy Watch 4 marking the switch to Wear OS. 

The new schedule will apparently see new Galaxy Watch releases every other year, pushing the next release into 2028. The report goes on to mention that Galaxy Watch is part of a “mature phase” of the smartwatch market, and that Galaxy Watch 9 sales “fell short of expectations” likely due in part to its higher price point. 

	

What’s next for Galaxy Watch?

Apparently, Samsung plans new Galaxy Watch software updates next year as well as “enhancement of healthcare features.” The Galaxy Fit 4 fitness tracker is also expected in 2027, with Dealabs reporting that the tracker will be priced at €79.90 in Europe, a slight price hike over the previous release.

snippet: Apple Pay is a go-to feature for iPhone users when shopping in stores, online, and in apps. Apple recently announced four new features that make Apple Pay even better. fullText:
Apple Pay is a go-to feature for iPhone users when shopping in stores, online, and in apps. Apple recently announced four new features that make Apple Pay even better. Here’s how they work, plus one major expansion that’s rolling out now. 

9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Score Sony’s INZONE noise-canceling earbuds for 38% off. These deliver immersive 360 Spatial Sound, active noise canceling, low-latency wireless connectivity, and much more.

New design in iOS 27

One of my favorite changes in iOS 27 is the redesigned Apple Pay checkout interface. The new interface makes it much easier to switch between different cards during the checkout flow on websites and in apps.

In the new design, you can easily swipe between cards on the main Apple Pay checkout screen. You can also tap on a card to view a grid of all your available Apple Pay cards.

The design also makes it easier to see information about individual cards, including rewards, balances, pay later options, and more.

iOS 27 was released to everyone last week. You can update in the Settings app on your iPhone. 

American Express rewards

Apple and American Express recently announced a new partnership that lets you pay with American Express rewards points.

When shopping online or in apps with an American Express card, you’ll see a new “Use Rewards” option alongside your available Membership Rewards points balance. You can apply points to cover all or part of your purchase, right in the Apple Pay checkout flow.

American Express points redeemed via Apple Pay are valued at 0.7 cents each. For example, this means 10,000 points can be redeemed for $70 applied towards your purchase.

In iOS 27, Apple is adding a new “Tap to Share” feature that integrates with Apple Pay on iPhone for in-store shopping.

This feature is an extension of Tap to Pay on iPhone. Apple explains:

With just a tap, customers can connect to a participating merchant’s iPhone for a more personalized and faster in-store purchase experience that allows for secure sharing of information, such as email and other contact information, shipping address, loyalty rewards information, and more.

Customers will also be able to view the items in their basket in real time so they can keep track of what they’ve purchased and ensure all sales and discounts are properly applied.

When done, shoppers can complete the checkout on their iPhone using Apple Pay.

Reload debit cards

iPhone users with select banks can manage their debit card balances directly in the Apple Pay interface. According to Apple, you’ll be able to use Apple Pay to add money to a supported debit card directly in Apple Wallet or when checking out.

Bonus: Apple Pay at Walmart 

This one isn’t really a new feature developed by Apple. Instead, it’s something that should’ve happened years ago finally coming to fruition. Walmart has announced that it is finally starting to roll out support for Apple Pay. Apple Pay is also rolling out to Sam’s Club as part of this initiative.  

As of November, Walmart’s roll out of Apple Pay across the United States is complete. 

Wrap up

As Apple Pay continues to increase in popularity and prevalence among retailers, it’s great to see Apple continue to improve the experience. Personally, Apple Pay is my checkout payment method of choice basically everywhere I shop — whether that’s online or in store.

How often do you use Apple Pay? What are your favorite Apple Pay features? Let us know down in the comments.

title: Yale’s Sonnenfeld: Nvidia is a ‘detriment’ to US industrial might — not a champion
snippet: Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld warns that what the market cheered Monday, Jensen Huang's White House–backed return as Nvidia's CEO and board member, could prove a giant mistake, exposing the directors to "historic" personal liability from a growing pile of lawsuits and raising the question of whether the country is celebrating a company that has helped put advanced chips in its adversaries' hands.
fullText:
Investors cheered Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia’s CEO on Monday, but renowned business academic Jeffrey Sonnenfeld of Yale thinks they’re celebrating a mistake. He sees a company that is largely responsible for putting sophisticated technology in the hands of the country’s adversaries, at a moment when the risks couldn’t be higher. Far from a champion of American industry, he says, Nvidia is “a detriment to U.S. global industrial might.”

As evidence, Sonnenfeld points to research suggesting Nvidia’s most advanced chips have reached China despite U.S. export controls and to sinking shares of Anthropic, which he links to the realization that China’s seemingly miraculous open source AI models are, in a sense, copies of top U.S. labs’ work, even as Nvidia has insisted that smuggling is a “non-factor.”

Indeed, Huang’s return was greeted with just as much enthusiasm in Asia, The Washington Post reported. “The king is back!” read one headline from China’s state-affiliated Star Market Daily.

The reinstatement itself followed heavy pressure from Washington. Nvidia’s chairman had effectively ruled out Huang’s return just last week. Then, in a torrent of private weekend calls led by Vice President JD Vance, top administration officials leaned on the board to welcome Huang back, with President Trump calling the board directly to vouch for him. “I made the deal,” Trump told CNBC on Monday.

Sonnenfeld says the directors who went along, and who returned Huang to the board even as it investigates whether foreign intelligence efforts targeted him, now face a “historic level of individual liability.”

The legal deluge has already begun. As we noted a couple of weeks ago, a potential class-action lawsuit was filed almost immediately. Days later, a shareholder derivative suit followed. Filed on Nvidia’s behalf against the directors themselves, the suit alleges the board ignored red flags about Huang’s relationship with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang.

The class action is very much aimed at making Nvidia and Huang compensate investors for their losses, while the derivative suit puts the directors’ own behavior on trial, with any recovery going to Nvidia. Three more suits followed on November 18, the day after Nvidia’s most recent earnings call; all five were filed in Northern California, where Nvidia is based.

Huang and Nvidia are also juggling a Justice Department antitrust investigation, a reported SEC probe into Nvidia’s accounting, a possible FBI review, a California subpoena, an export-control case that landed partner Megaspeed on the U.S. trade blacklist on Monday, and congressional inquiries, including a Senate Banking hearing next week at which Huang has agreed to testify.

Here’s more of what Sonnenfeld had to say, in a Q&A that’s been edited for length and clarity.

So much has happened since we last talked. Huang was ousted, he’s come back. Do you think the board’s reliance on government assurances here is defensible or an abdication of its own duties?

They failed to rely on experts. That’s one of the reasons this board is going to be sued and lose, and these directors are likely to face a historic level of individual liability. They have a very inadequate directors and officers liability policy. They have also just failed in their diligence. They hired the Wachtell [law] firm. The Wachtell firm barely got off the blocks to do an investigation. And then they have already reversed themselves, so they didn’t use the expertise needed.

It’s wild that they also put Huang right back on the board of directors.

The board showed, in addition to incompetence and collaboration, just cowardice in their capitulation because Trump has nothing to wave over them. If this was SpaceX, where 46% of its business comes from the government [you could maybe see the case for Trump’s involvement]. For Nvidia, it’s not even 1% of its business that comes from the U.S. government, so [the board] didn’t have that threat. [Trump] can call off [federal] investigations, but he can’t call off the shareholder litigation. Some are already filed, and the estimates are there’ll probably be 30 of them, and they’re going to be extremely costly.

And this is not, by the way, just a blue or red state issue. We already have 14 GOP senators who’ve already come out against this, and very prominent conservatives, like Pete Ricketts and Josh Hawley and Tom Cotton and John Cornyn. Those are some issues that may help explain why Nvidia’s stock is tumbling today.

Might the board say, “We saw the classified intelligence findings, and they assure us Jensen will be absolved of wrongdoing”?

They haven’t seen those findings, and we also haven’t seen what will be the result of the Senate Intelligence Committee, the Senate Special Committee on Investigations, the Senate Banking Committee, and all their House counterparts. The board hasn’t seen any of that, and even if they saw it, which they have not yet, that still wouldn’t matter.

Do you think the Commerce Department will continue to tighten its chip export controls to keep China from accessing so much compute or walk back some of those recent moves?

We already see that Megaspeed has finally been put on the sanctions list, as it should have been before. And we have documentation now that Nvidia, rather than a champion of U.S. global industrial might, is actually a detriment to U.S. global industrial might, because their chips have now turned out to be in the hands and in the systems of not just the Chinese military, as they got channeled to Northwestern Polytechnical University, which is a military institution — this is going into weapons that will, of course, be funneled to Iran and Russia, and they didn’t have access to that a year ago. [Editor’s note: China has long denied supplying weapons to either country. Nvidia chips have been found in Russian drones, however, and the U.S. ambassador to China said in September that President Trump had discussed selling arms to China, an account Trump has denied.]

The open source models that people have celebrated and marveled at — that China somehow has this ingenuity to be creating their own chips, so that Kimi and DeepSeek and these other celebrated open source models were producing a miracle of Anthropic-like results — turns out we know why. They are pirating it. They are “distilling it” from Anthropic using high-end Nvidia chips.

Nvidia has denied reports that its most advanced chips have been smuggled into China.

There’s an Israeli company, Lava, that just three weeks ago showed [dozens of] Blackwell chips are in China. We’re seeing, with the return of Jensen Huang, Anthropic plummet. Why would that be? Of course, this is because it’s hurting OpenAI. It’s hurting Grok. It’s hurting Perplexity. It’s hurting Gemini. And you’ve seen none of these tech titans celebrate this. We have the misogynist tech bros holding locker-room-type rallies about Jensen Huang’s return, but nobody else has spoken out in favor of this. [You’re not hearing from] the CEOs of Microsoft or IBM or J.P. Morgan or Walmart or General Motors or Caterpillar. Nobody thinks that this is a good move.

You don’t think Nvidia needed Huang back?

He was not the guy designing the chips. It’s important to point out that that’s a guy named Chris Malachowsky, a co-founder who’s still there who designed these GPUs and has a whole team of next-generation people like Jonah Alben doing the chip design. As for the great software that has leveraged these chips, that’s also not Jensen Huang. That’s a guy named Ian Buck, who’s been very much celebrated in the last two weeks. He’s the one who designed the CUDA software that leverages the chips. Those people weren’t going anywhere, and wherever Jensen Huang is has nothing to do with them. 

Some are trying to make Huang’s forced resignation about the extramarital affairs to which he has admitted, calling it HR policy gone wild. 

A CEO who doesn’t stand by his own code of conduct makes it completely unenforceable. 

Wired quoted an Nvidia employee who said they’d never take an HR training course again if Huang was reinstated.

This thing is a sexual affair with a subordinate — whether it’s coercion, or even if it truly was somehow consensual, it’s not fair. Every decision on resource allocation, on staffing, on product decisions, is not objective. It’s either favoritism, or, if the relationship fails, retribution. All the other people on that team rise and fall with a sexual relationship; it’s something they have no control over.

CNET’s Lori Grunin prefers the Legion Go S with SteamOS over the Steam Deck OLED. You’ll get an 8-inch display on the Legion Go S, which is larger than the display on the Steam Deck OLED. The display can refresh at up to 120Hz, so fast-moving games will look smoother. This one runs SteamOS, which will give you a console-like interface and quick access to your Steam library.

You’ll get a Ryzen Z1 Extreme processor and 32GB of RAM with this configuration, which will help with more demanding games. Lenovo is offering free delivery and a price match guarantee, and you can return the Legion Go S until Jan. 27. You can also grab the Legion Go S carry case at checkout, where the case is down to $8, from $20. We don’t know how long Lenovo’s stock will last, so you should order soon if you want the Legion Go S at $850.

			

	

You would have paid $900 for this Legion Go S configuration at launch, and as much as $1,608 after that as gaming component costs rise. At $850, you’ll be paying $50 less than the launch price. 

Alternatives you might like

	

		

	

									

									

						

		

				

			Nintendo/CNET		

	

		

							

											

							Best overall gaming handheld						

											

															Nintendo Switch 2													

									

			

	

		

		

			Get it now		

	

		
		

			

The Nintendo Switch 2 is our pick for the best overall gaming handheld, with a CNET score of 8.5 out of 10. The Switch 2 has a slim design with a large 1080p display, and the controllers attach magnetically. We got less battery life from the Switch 2 than from the original Switch in our testing. Nintendo only lets you play games bought on game cards or through the eShop, so you won’t be able to bring your Steam library to the Switch 2.

		

	

	

		

	

									

									

						

		

				

			Valve/CNET		

	

		

							

											

							Best PC handheld						

											

															Steam Deck OLED													

									

			

	

		

		

			Get it now		

	

		
		

			

Valve’s Steam Deck OLED uses the same SteamOS software as the Legion Go S. The Steam Deck OLED has an HDR OLED display, and we liked the controls and the improved haptics in our testing. Valve is selling the Steam Deck OLED for $789, which is $61 less than the Legion Go S. The Steam Deck OLED has a smaller screen than the Legion Go S, though, so you’ll have to decide if the $61 saving makes up for the difference in size.

		

	

	

		

	

									

									

						

		

				

			Asus/CNET		

	

		

							

											

							Best Windows gaming handheld						

											

															Asus ROG Xbox Ally X													

									

			

	

		

		

			Get it now		

	

		
		

			

The ROG Xbox Ally X runs Windows, so you can install games from multiple game stores without any workarounds. The grips are larger than the ones on most handhelds, which can make the ROG Xbox Ally X more comfortable to hold. We found the performance to be excellent in lighter games, but Windows can sometimes slow the handheld down. At $1,000 at Best Buy, the ROG Xbox Ally X is $150 more expensive than the Legion Go S.

		

	

Is Black Friday a good time to buy a gaming handheld?

It depends on the handheld. Lenovo has cut the Legion Go S with SteamOS to $850, from $1,608, for Black Friday. But we haven’t found Black Friday discounts on the Nintendo Switch 2, the Steam Deck OLED or the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X yet. You’ll find more discounts in other categories right now, including Best Buy’s Black Friday OLED TV deals and our Black Friday headphone deals.

Should I buy the Legion Go S now or wait for Black Friday?

You likely won’t gain much by waiting. Lenovo has labeled the $850 price a doorbuster, and we don’t know how long the stock will last. Best Buy’s Black Friday sale recently had the same model for $901, which is $51 more than Lenovo’s price. Lenovo is also offering a price match guarantee and extended returns through Jan. 27, in case you find a lower price during Amazon’s Black Friday sale or Walmart’s Black Friday sale.

Is the Legion Go S with SteamOS better than the Steam Deck OLED?

CNET Senior Editor Lori Grunin prefers the Legion Go S with SteamOS, which has a larger display and a different control layout. The Steam Deck OLED is still our pick for the best PC handheld on our list of the best handheld gaming consoles, and it’s the one I would buy myself. The Steam Deck OLED has an HDR OLED display, while the Legion Go S has an LCD screen. The Legion Go S and the Steam Deck OLED both use SteamOS, so you should be able to play most of the same Steam games on either handheld.

title: HBO Max’s Black Friday Deal Gets You a Year of DC, ‘Harry Potter,’ ‘The Pitt’ and More for Half Off
snippet: HBO Max’s Basic with Ads plan is now $5.50 a month for Black Friday.
fullText:
Black Friday week is full of epic shopping bargains, and when it comes to streaming, there are plenty of deals to consider. HBO Max is currently offering a whopping 50% off a full year of its ad-supported plan. If you’ve been waiting to catch up on every episode of DC’s Lanterns and A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, your time has arrived.

Between Nov. 23 and Nov. 30, you can get HBO Max’s Basic with Ads subscription for the monthly price of $5.50 (it is normally $11 a month). New and eligible returning subscribers can take advantage of this deal, which offers $66 in savings for the year.

To get this deal, you can sign up directly on the streamer’s website. Or, if you want to subscribe directly through Prime Video and have it as an add-on subscription, Amazon has included this offering as part of its Black Friday deals as well.

			

More from CNET

title: Wispr Flow improves dictation accuracy with new Canto-2 speech-to-text model
snippet: Popular AI dictation app Wispr Flow is rolling out a new speech-to-text model for Mac, iPhone, and other platforms, promising fewer transcription errors and better recognition of names and technical terms. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Popular AI dictation app Wispr Flow is rolling out a new speech-to-text model for Mac, iPhone, and other platforms, promising fewer transcription errors and better recognition of names and technical terms. Here are the details.

Wispr Flow rolls out Canto-2 model

Wispr Flow this week launched Canto-2, its newest speech-to-text model, which the company says reduces transcription errors by 36% across 14 languages and by more than 15% in English compared to its predecessor, Canto-1.

In practice, that means the average error rate dropped from 9.9% to 6.3% across the 14 languages, and from 3.2% to 2.7% in English, according to Wispr’s internal benchmarks.

According to the company, teaching a model to recognize specific names and terms comes with a trade-off: the more it relies on that user-specific context, the more likely it is to insert those words even when they weren’t actually spoken.

Wispr notes that Canto-2 strikes a better balance between context and accuracy, improving its ability to recognize user-specific terms without substantially increasing the frequency of incorrect substitutions:

Canto-2 recovers hard names and terms accurately nearly 7 of 10 times, without more false insertions. It makes a third fewer mistakes across 14 languages, and has the lowest Hindi error rate of any multilingual model on Hugging Face’s open benchmark. It is 10 times the scale of Canto-1, and our biggest step yet toward dictation that’s ready to send without a single edit.

According to the company, the percentage of difficult names and terms correctly recognized went from 41% to 69% between Canto-1 and Canto-2, “without inserting them more often.” It added that this improvement holds up even as the user’s custom dictionary grows, with the new model correctly recognizing 92% of easier terms even with 1,000 saved entries.

Wispr also noted that it trained Canto-2 to handle real-world dictation conditions, including background noise, laptop and phone microphones, and sentences that restart halfway through, rather than relying solely on clean recordings of scripted speech.

When tested using Hugging Face’s public multilingual benchmark, Canto-2 achieved results that would have placed it third overall as of November 9. However, Wispr conducted the evaluation itself, and the model has not yet been officially added to the leaderboard as of today, November 25.

In its own internal benchmarks, the company says Canto-2 achieved the lowest average error rate among the competing models it tested across 14 languages.

Canto-2 is now available to Wispr Flow users on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android in the Americas, with the rollout to other regions underway.

title: Google Meet unlocks 1080p video streaming for all accounts on web
snippet: Streaming in 1080p will be the default in Google Meet, regardless of whether you pay for Google Workspace. That includes personal Google Accounts. more…
fullText:
Streaming in 1080p will be the default in Google Meet, regardless of whether you pay for Google Workspace. That includes personal Google Accounts.

Google says users will default to sending and receiving 1080p video, at the minimum. Previously, Google Meet made 720p the standard for streaming, and a higher resolution had historically been locked behind the Google One 2TB plan. That’s been true since 1080p streaming was rolled out in 2023.

The upgrade will roll out to everyone, including those with Google Workspace accounts and personal Google Accounts. The only requirement to stream your own 1080p video in Google Meet for web will be hardware-based. Google’s press release states that devices with cameras capable of streaming in high definition will do so, and the feature will be turned on automatically.

It can be disabled, though. Users can head to Settings > Video in Google Meet for web. Video will also appear in a lower resolution if the user’s video tile is shrunk down on-screen.

	

The update appears to be centered on web-only instances of Google Meet, and might not include the app on Android or iOS. For the time being, those versions may still be limited to streaming in 720p for those who don’t have an active Google One subscription.

Google Meet started its extended rollout of 1080p streaming to everyone earlier this month, so it shouldn’t be much longer until the change has taken place completely.

Claude launches Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides integration with sidebar and more

title: Screens can now turn iPhone Duo into a tiny MacBook
snippet: Screens 5.10 delivered two highly-requested desktop features to users earlier this month. Now the app is back with a fun update for iPhone Duo users: tiny laptop mode. more…
fullText:
Screens 5.10 delivered two highly-requested desktop features to users earlier this month. Now the app is back with a fun update for iPhone Duo users: tiny laptop mode.

iPhone Duo supports various positions including a partially opened configuration. iOS 27 allows apps to respond to the hinge position, offering unique experiences as a result.

Edovia, the makers of Screens, took this as an opportunity to make the remote desktop viewer transform iPhone Duo into what it looks like in this mode: a very miniature notebook computer.

“Simply fold your iPhone Duo halfway to turn it into a pocket-sized workstation, with your remote desktop on the upper half and a custom keyboard and trackpad below,” Edovia says.

“The trackpad supports the same familiar gestures you’ve come to expect from Screens, while the custom keyboard supports multiple languages, follows your selected system keyboard language, and lets you swipe down on keys to access secondary characters, just like on iPad.”

They show off the update in full on their website here. Screens for iPhone Duo is available on the App Store.

snippet: We reviewed dozens of products in 2026, and the one through line across all of them was cost. fullText:
We reviewed dozens of products in 2026, and the one through line across all of them was cost. Because of RAMageddon, everything was more expensive, and it became somewhat easier to separate the products that were good because they were cheap from the ones that were good at any price.

This year was a lot of things, but it was primarily a reminder that the best products are created through careful iteration. Only one product on this list, the XREAL Aura, represents an emerging class. The rest, from the Fitbit Air to the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, showcase years of work in optimizing for design, weight, battery life, and performance. Some take more risks than others, but to us they all represent the very best of their respective categories.

Fitbit Air

Price: $99.99/$129.99 (special editions)

Black Friday deal: Save $30 on the Google Fitbit Air Champagne Gold & Obsidian Bundle. Ends 12/02.

Release date: May 26, 2026

A screenless Google device outside of a smart speaker wasn’t something I thought I needed. Yet the Fitbit Air has become one of my favorite products to come out of Mountain View in years. Fitness tracking is something I want happening quietly in the background, not another reason to check a screen.

	

That’s what the Air gets right. It isn’t trying to reinvent fitness tracking; it packages it in a comfortable, lightweight band that stays out of the way. Health tracking data isn’t locked behind a paywall, and there’s no display demanding attention throughout the day.

Smart rings and full-featured watches have their place, but this slim wearable strikes a particularly appealing balance. It gives me useful information when I want it without becoming another device to manage. It’s comfortable, inexpensive, and easy to live with—and sometimes that’s exactly what makes a product great.

— Damien Wilde, Daniel Bader & Andrew Romero

XGIMI Horizon 30 Pro

Price: $2,499

Black Friday price: $1,899

Release date: November 1, 2026

I’m primarily a TV person, especially when it comes to gaming. But after spending time with XGIMI’s Horizon 30 Pro, I’ve been enjoying a very different setup. I loved the older Horizon Pro 4K and used it until this arrived; the 30 Pro feels like a substantial leap forward.

VRR support has made it possible to play my Steam Machine on a roughly 200-inch image in the bedroom, while the built-in speakers do an impressive job of filling the room. Going from Forza Horizon 5 at 120fps to Blue Planet on BBC iPlayer is effortless thanks to Google TV.

The swiveling base is more useful than it might sound. I can position the projector in the corner of the room and let XGIMI’s keystone correction handle the rest. It’s an expensive upgrade, but for a home cinema setup that doubles as a giant gaming display, it’s a beast.

— Damien Wilde

Steam Controller (2026)

Price: $99

Release date: May 4, 2026

I still wish the Steam Controller cost less. Beyond that, though, I have very little to complain about: this is the best controller I’ve used in years. It’s comfortable, gives Windows users a way to control their PC, and brings together some of the best ideas from my beloved Steam Deck.

Steam Input is the real selling point. The depth of customization makes this controller feel at home on a PC in a way few alternatives do. I haven’t connected with a new controller this quickly in a long time.

That doesn’t mean everyone needs one. Most people would be well served by an 8BitDo controller—or even a Stadia controller converted to Bluetooth. But if you play on PC and want the premium option, this is my pick.

— Damien Wilde

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8

Price: $1,899.99

Black Friday price: $1,549.99

Release date: August 7, 2026

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is my favorite foldable of 2026. I’ve been enthralled with its design since reviewing it in July, and it won’t be leaving my daily rotation anytime soon.

The short, compact outer screen is refreshing to use, but it’s the inner display that changed the way I think about foldables. Its proportions feel more flexible than the square-shaped displays that have become so common across the category. Samsung’s motivations for adopting this form factor may be obvious, but the result works—and that’s what matters when I’m using it every day.

— Ben Schoon, Daniel Bader & Andrew Romero

Nothing Ear (3) / Ear (3a)

Price: Ear (3): $179 / Ear (3a): $99

Black Friday price: Ear (3): $94 / Ear (3a): $69

Release date: Ear (3): Sept 18, 2025 / Ear (3a): July 7, 2026

Ear (3a) earns the nod here, but this is really a celebration of Nothing’s entire audio lineup. Its clean sound profiles, thoughtful designs, and compatibility with Android and the other devices I use have kept me listening all year.

Ear (3) remains my primary pair of earbuds, while Ear (3a) gets plenty of use when pocket space is at a premium. Ear (open) and Nothing Headphone (1) Pro round out the rest of my listening needs.

I still stand by calling Ear (3a) simply ‘the best earbuds.’ More broadly, Nothing has built an audio lineup worth paying attention to, especially when end-of-year discounts make it easier to try.

— Ben Schoon

Oppo Find X9 Ultra

Price: ~$1,999

Release date: April 21, 2026 (China) / Nov 2026 (Global)

If there’s one phone from 2026 I wish I could return to, it’s the Oppo Find X9 Ultra. ColorOS has quietly become one of the best Android experiences by getting the small details right, and the Ultra’s camera hardware and shooting experience remain standouts—even next to Oppo’s newer Find X10 Pro Max.

This is one of those increasingly rare smartphones that feels unwilling to compromise. I’ll be thinking about it until there’s a proper successor, and the prospect of not getting one in 2027 is disappointing.

I wish Oppo had sold this phone officially in the US. Importing comes with real complications, but the Find X9 Ultra is one of the few phones good enough to make me consider it.

— Ben Schoon

Honor Magic V6

Price: ~$1,720

Release date: March 13, 2026

It’s been a remarkable year for foldables, but the Honor Magic V6 is my favorite of the bunch. Its combination of durability, battery life, and camera quality finally made me stop thinking about going back to a conventional slab phone.

The cameras are a big part of that. I used to rely entirely on my Panasonic GH5 for work photos; now I often reach for the Magic V6 instead. Its large 1/2-inch telephoto sensor helps it deliver the kind of dependable results I want when I need to capture something quickly.

It’s also held up to far more punishment than I’d normally put a foldable through. After a mud torture test and a trip through the dishwasher, I’m still using it months later. Battery life has been another major strength.

Honor’s software still has rough edges, but the improvements are substantial, and the seven-year update promise matters. The remaining problem is availability: I’d love to see Honor make its phones officially accessible across North America.

— Nicholas Sutrich

XREAL Aura

Price: $1,099

Release date: November 2026

Android XR has had an awkward start, but the XREAL Aura feels like the kind of product the platform needed from the beginning. It puts a fresh idea into a form factor that’s easier to imagine wearing than a bulky headset.

Think of it as smart glasses that behave more like a VR headset. Open the app drawer with a pinch—or use the tethered compute puck—and your chosen app appears as a floating window you can move around. It’s like having a tablet suspended wherever you need it.

That makes remote work and entertainment feel surprisingly natural, especially when the glasses weigh less than a fifth of many VR headsets. There are compromises: hand gestures can be finicky, and while Bluetooth game controllers work, there isn’t a Meta Quest-style motion controller available for immersive gaming.

Even so, Aura makes a compelling case for Android XR. It’s an appealing option for people interested in immersive entertainment who don’t want the weight and bulk of a conventional VR headset.

— Nicholas Sutrich

DroidDeck

Price: Free

DroidDeck has changed the way I think about gaming on Android. It isn’t the first project to bring PC games to a phone, but it feels like one of the most capable. The pitch is straightforward, even if the technology isn’t: run Steam on your Android device.

Rather than emulating an entire PC in the traditional sense, DroidDeck brings together translation layers using projects such as FEX and Proton. The technical details are complicated, but the practical result is that your phone can run games it wasn’t originally designed to understand.

Performance across my devices has been impressive—good enough that I’ve seen games run better than on my Steam Deck. The project is also free, community-driven, and highly customizable. The trade-off is that support for brand-new hardware can take time.

If you’ve been on the fence about mobile gaming, pairing DroidDeck with a controller such as my favorite, the GameSir G8 Galileo, is a great way to see how far it’s come.

Download DroidDeck

— Nicholas Sutrich

Fitbit Edge

Price: $179.99 / $219.99 (special editions)

Release date: October 27, 2026

The Fitbit Air is a good fitness tracker and, to my eye, an attractive bracelet. But years of wearing watches have trained me to expect the time on my wrist. Even toward the end of my time with the Air, I kept glancing down for a clock that wasn’t there.

The Fitbit Edge fixes that central complaint. Its always-on display reduces battery life to roughly two or three days, but that’s a trade-off I’m happy to make. The software’s Pixel Watch-inspired look also helps it feel like part of a more cohesive lineup. For me, a small screen makes a meaningful difference.

— Abner Li

Google Pixel Tag

Price: $29.99

Release date: November 11, 2026

We waited so long for a first-party Google tracker that the Find My Device network had time to become Find Hub. The Pixel Tag makes the wait worthwhile with a more integrated experience: everything is managed in the Find Hub app, rather than spread across separate software.

‘Notify when left behind’ was overdue, and ‘Ring this phone’ has worked well for me. These are practical features, but they’re also reminders of how much first-party hardware can do to improve the software around it.

I also like the pill-shaped design. Google didn’t simply copy the AirTag; it made something that feels at home in the Pixel family. It’s a small thing, but it’s pleasant to hold—and surprisingly satisfying to fidget with.

— Abner Li

Keychron Thunderbolt 5 Dock (14-in-1)

Price: $349.99

Black Friday price: $314.99

Release date: July 6, 2026

A dock needs to do more than look good, but Keychron’s Thunderbolt 5 dock makes a strong first impression on a desk. Its machined aluminum case fits neatly into my setup, and the usefulness goes well beyond the finish.

I switched between devices more often this year. Moving my work from a Windows PC to the Mac mini M6 left the PC on gaming duty, while the Googlebook launch gave me another computer to plug into the same monitors and workstation.

The Keychron dock makes those changes simple: I connect the USB-C input cable and let it handle the display and data connections. Its own power supply, four USB-A ports, three USB-C ports, SD card reader, and wired Ethernet connection give me the flexibility I need. It might be the most useful addition I’ve made to my desk all year.

— Andrew Romero

Onyx Boox Picco

Price: $109.99

Release date: October 2026

I don’t think I’ll stop talking about the Boox Picco anytime soon. It’s a wonderfully simple little e-reader with a straightforward operating system and battery life that stretches across days or weeks, depending on use.

You can attach it magnetically to the back of your phone or slip it into almost any pocket. But the bigger benefit is how easy it makes picking up a book, whether I’m out of the house or just moving from one room to another.

At around $100, it’s an appealingly focused device. In a year when so much attention has gone to retro gadgets and handhelds, the Picco captures a similar pleasure: a small piece of technology that does one thing well.

— Andrew Romero

Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro

Price: $499.99

Black Friday price: $399.99

Release date: October 14, 2026

If one gadget came out of nowhere to steal the show for me in 2026, it was the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro. Amazon rebooted its tablet lineup, dropped the Fire branding, and embraced a much more familiar version of Android. Install a third-party launcher to remove the permanent Alexa search bar, and it feels like a regular mid-range Android tablet—with full Play Store support, no sideloading required.

The hardware is where it really wins me over. The base configuration pairs 8GB of RAM with 128GB of storage, which is more than enough for browsing, movies, YouTube, and casual games. But the display is the standout: this is a much better LCD than I expect from a tablet under $1,000, and the nanomatte finish looks and feels fantastic.

I’m as surprised as anyone that Amazon finally figured out its tablet lineup. A little help from the person behind Microsoft’s Surface line seems to have gone a long way. At this price—and especially on sale—I struggle to recommend anything else, including Apple’s base iPad. It’s that good.

— Will Sattelberg

XTEINK X4 Pro

Price: $99

Black Friday price: $84

Release date: July 21, 2026

I have always been a reader, but in my effort to spend less time on my phone this year, I did my utmost to return to e-paper displays for most long-form reading.

The XTEINK X4 Pro is a tiny 4-inch touch-capable e-paper display with a backlight and plenty of battery life. Its magnets help the device stick to the back of most phones (though it’s a bit tall for some smaller devices like the Pixel 11 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro), and it supports custom firmware through the Crosspoint project.

While it occasionally feels cramped to read on, the sheer number of formatting and font options makes it easy to adjust the reading experience to suit your tastes. And because it supports KOReader, reading progress syncs with most other devices, including Kobo e-readers and supported phone apps.

— Daniel Bader

BMX SolidSafe Duo

One of the biggest challenges with the iPhone Duo is finding a MagSafe battery pack that actually fits the shorter, wider form factor. That is where the BMX SolidSafe Duo comes into play.  It was purpose-built for the iPhone Duo. You get:

What makes this thing so nice is that not only can you charge your iPhone Duo, but it also has an integrated stand, which is a must for viewing content on the inner display. I’m also a sucker for a diagnostics display.

New hybrid foam and silicone ear tips

Up to eight hours of listening with ANC on and up to 24 hours with the included case

Built-in heart rate sensor

All the ecosystem features like:

Auto switching

Live translation

Transparency mode

Live listen

& more

title: Apple has iPads running macOS already, but don’t get too excited
snippet: With iPads running the same chips as Macs, many have wished Apple would give us the option of running macOS on them instead of the somewhat clunky iPadOS windowing system. Apple’s previous arguments against converging devices have been somewhat weakened by the launch of the touchscreen MacBook Pro. A new report says that Apple already has iPads running macOS internally, and that work on a giant iPad continues, but don’t hold your breath for a public launch of either … more…
fullText:
With iPads running the same chips as Macs, many have wished Apple would give us the option of running macOS on them instead of the somewhat clunky iPadOS windowing system. Apple’s previous arguments against converging devices have been somewhat weakened by the launch of the touchscreen MacBook Pro.

A new report says that Apple already has iPads running macOS internally, and that work on a giant iPad continues, but don’t hold your breath for a public launch of either … 

As iPad hardware has grown more powerful over the years, the software has struggled to keep up. We saw split-screen capabilities first, with full windowing finally coming to the devices in iPadOS 26 last year.

The UI is still rather clunky compared to macOS, however, leading a significant number of people to wish that Apple simply offered the option of using the more powerful operating system on its tablet devices.

	

In a podcast Q&A, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says that Apple is already doing this internally, but there’s no sign of any plans to make it available outside the company.

Apple has iPads internally running macOS, and they’ve had that for some time. The fact that they have the underlying architecture of Apple Silicon that’s the same on the iPad and the Mac gives them the flexibility in order to test these types of things.

In terms if they’re actually going to do it – would they bring macOS to the iPad itself – at this point I don’t think that’s going to happen anytime soon. I’ve checked into this and there’s no ongoing operating system project right now in terms of a brand new operating system for the iPad – there is no work being done to consumerize macOs on the iPad.

Gurman says Apple seems set to continue to make piecemeal changes over time to bring iPad capabilities closer to those of the Mac but is showing no signs of full convergence.

He reiterated that work on a long-rumored giant-sized folding iPad continues.

The other thing I want to say is that I’m really excited for this potential of Project J312. That is, this giant 19-inch, 20-inch foldable iPad. And it’s basically like a gigantic iPhone Duo with no display on the outside.

However, he says there’s no guarantee it will ever launch, saying the timings have already slipped from 2027 through 2028 to 2029, but both cost and yield issues may still kill the project. If it does launch, it’s expected to cost anywhere from $3,000 to $5,000.

title: MacBook Neo 2 likely to launch around March, could feature new colors: report
snippet: One of Apple’s most beloved products this year was undoubtedly the MacBook Neo. Unlike some of its other budget products, Apple seems interested in updating the MacBook Neo on an annual cycle, and we may get the next MacBook Neo around March. more…
fullText:
One of Apple’s most beloved products this year was undoubtedly the MacBook Neo. Unlike some of its other budget products, Apple seems interested in updating the MacBook Neo on an annual cycle, and we may get the next MacBook Neo around March.

Apple targeting iOS 27.4 cycle for new budget products

According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple is targeting the iOS/macOS 27.4 release cycle for the release of the new MacBook Neo, as well as the A19 budget iPad, iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and OLED iPad Air.

While he notes that this cycle runs between February and March, it doesn’t necessarily mean the products will launch on the earlier end of that spectrum. Apple is also expected to release the iPhone Air 2, OLED iPad Air, and a new iPad Pro within the first half of the year, but they’ll likely come a bit later than the aforementioned products.

MacBook Neo 2 upgrades

As expected, the next MacBook Neo will bump up from the A18 Pro chip with 8GB of RAM to the A19 Pro chip with 12GB of RAM.

Apple will also introduce new colors on the MacBook Neo “frequently,” though it’s unclear if we’ll see that with the next iteration. From the Power On newsletter:

The other thing I’ve heard is that Apple plans to refresh the MacBook Neo’s colors frequently. We’ll see if that trend starts with the first follow-up.

Wrap up

I’m certainly excited to see the next generation MacBook Neo, especially with 12GB of unified memory. While 8GB is certainly fine, heavy multitaskers will notice it, especially with unoptimized software.

The bigger question is: will the next MacBook Neo have a price increase? With additional RAM included, it feels inevitable. 

	

Apple increased the price of MacBook Neo from $599 to $699 back in June, and in October the company also silently decreased the education discount by $50, meaning the education price has increased from $499 to $649 since launch.

If there is a price increase, it likely won’t be too major, maybe $50 – leaving the computer at $749. Compared to the rest of the laptop landscape, MacBook Neo would still be a good value. We’ll see what happens.

snippet: Recently, UGREEN introduced a new Qi2.2 25W 10000mAh MagSafe battery bank for iPhone. There have been plenty of these, but this one has an interesting new twist: liquid cooling. For Black Friday, it’s on sale for 40% off, making it more affordable than ever. more…
fullText:
Recently, UGREEN introduced a new Qi2.2 25W 10000mAh MagSafe battery bank for iPhone. There have been plenty of these, but this one has an interesting new twist: liquid cooling. For Black Friday, it’s on sale for 40% off, making it more affordable than ever.

On the back of the battery, there’s a window that showcases the liquid within the battery bank moving throughout it. This should help keep it a little bit cooler than most MagSafe battery banks.

UGREEN says that it’ll be around 18 degrees cooler than usual, and while that’s probably true – it’s worth nothing that it still isn’t a cold battery bank, it’s just cooler than usual. It’ll still feel warm in your hand.

iOS 28 is coming next year, and a new rumor says the update will “revamp the iPhone’s notification system.” This comes as Android has introduced features like “Notification Organizer” to help users sort notifications into different categories.

9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Score Sony’s INZONE noise-canceling earbuds for 38% off. These deliver immersive 360 Spatial Sound, active noise canceling, low-latency wireless connectivity, and much more.

The report cites “multiple sources” and comes from MacRumors. There aren’t any specific details about what changes iOS 28 will introduce for notifications. “The sources said iOS 28 will include significant changes to Notification Center, but we do not have any specific details,” the report says.

The iOS notifications system is overdue for an update. While Apple has added features like Apple Intelligence-based priority notifications and notification summaries, the system still lacks other organization and sorting settings.

Android 16 introduced several significant notification changes, focused primarily on reducing clutter and prioritizing important information. For Pixel devices, the update also introduced Notification Organizer, a feature that automatically groups and silences low-priority alerts, including promotions, news, and social media notifications.

As Abner explained on 9to5Google last year:

The Notification Organizer will sort your alerts into the following categories: Promotions, News, Social, and Suggested. The first two are already on, but you must enable the remaining ones. There’s also an option to “Always expand bundles.”

I’d love for Apple to adopt a similar system on iPhone, iPad, and Mac. Even with the recent Apple Intelligence additions, the iOS notifications system is still far too basic.

title: The Best Foldable Phones to Give This Holiday Season
snippet: For the tech enthusiast in your life, a foldable phone could be an interesting alternative to a traditional smartphone. We’ve rounded up our top picks, from book-style designs to flip phones.
fullText:
If you’re shopping for someone this holiday season who deserves something a little more special — and you’ve got the budget to spare — a foldable phone can be a unique and practical gift that your loved one will use long after the holidays are over. 

After reviewing our fair share of foldable phones, we’ve narrowed down our top three picks for the holidays and the perfect person on your list for each one. Who knows, you might end up caving in and treating yourself to a brand-new device? (You’ve been warned.) 

For more mobile gift ideas, from budget-friendly smartphones to wearable devices, be sure to check out the video below.

		

			

iPhone Duo: Great for the Apple fan in your life

The iPhone Duo has a 5.4-inch cover display with a Ceramic Shield 2 covering to protect against scratches.Abrar Al-Heeti/CNET

The iPhone Duo is far from the first foldable phone, but as Apple’s debut into the market, it’s generated plenty of buzz. The Duo’s superpower is its ability to integrate hardware and software, creating a seamless experience across both displays. 

The compact, 5.4-inch cover screen is great for sending texts and emails and checking notifications. The more expansive 7.6-inch inner display is ideal for multitasking, watching movies and working. It feels like using a smaller version of an iPad Mini that you can just fold up and toss in your pocket or bag.

The Duo is a great gift for someone who’s said they want a foldable phone, but refused to get one of the long-standing Android options already on the market. At last, Apple has its own offering that lets you stick with iOS. It’s a handy pick for people who often work on their phones and don’t always want to lug around a laptop. It’s also good for anyone who watches a lot of movies and TV shows on their mobile device. Plus, as a phone-tablet hybrid, it’s just fun to use. 

The iPhone Duo has a 7.6-inch matte inner display to reduce glare.Abrar Al-Heeti/CNET

The iPhone Duo isn’t perfect. It doesn’t support Face ID, but Apple did recently add an option to unlock the phone using the front camera. This isn’t as secure as Face ID, so you’ll still need to use Touch ID or a passcode for more sensitive functions like using Apple Pay or accessing passwords, and after around 45 minutes of inactivity. 

The Duo’s cameras also aren’t as advanced as what you’ll get with the iPhone 18 Pro models, which have larger main-camera sensors and more advanced optical zoom capabilities. There’s also no telephoto camera on the Duo. Still, most people will be happy with the Duo’s 48-megapixel wide and ultrawide rear cameras, as well as the 12-megapixel selfie camera on the cover screen. The FaceTime camera on the inner display is best suited for video calls rather than snapping quality photos. 

Multitasking on the Duo is seamless, but it’s not as flexible as it is on other foldable phones. You can only have two apps open side by side, and you can’t readjust them. 

Perhaps the biggest downside is the price. The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 for 256GB of storage. That’s why it’s a good idea to keep an eye out for any deals that can help lower the price.  

Galaxy Z Fold 8: Best foldable for Android lovers

Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 is compact and versatile.Andrew Lanxon/CNET

For the Android-lover in your life, there’s no better foldable pick than Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8. Like the iPhone Duo, this phone has a passport-size design. (Technically, Samsung beat Apple to the punch, but let’s refrain from the “Who Did It First?” game for now.)

The Z Fold 8 has a 5.5-inch cover screen and a 7.6-inch inner display that’s great for watching videos, working and multitasking with up to three apps, which you can resize to your liking.

It’s also very thin, measuring 9.7mm thick when folded and 4.5mm thick when unfolded. That means it feels similar in thickness to a standard nonfolding phone, even when it’s closed. The Z Fold 8 fits squarely in a palm and easily slides into a pocket – tiny women’s pockets included.

The Z Fold 8 has a tablet-like 7.6-inch inner display.Andrew Lanxon/CNET

Like the iPhone Duo, the Z Fold 8 doesn’t have a telephoto camera. But the 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras on the back and the 10-megapixel selfie cameras do a solid job. 

The Z Fold 8 is also priced on the higher end, starting at $1,900 for 256GB. But its compact, sleek design and versatility help to make up for that sticker shock. Again, it’s a good idea to look out for any deals, especially around the holidays.

Motorola Razr 2026: A flip phone for nostalgists

The 2026 Motorola Razr has a 3.6-inch cover display that’s good for quickly checking apps.David Lumb/CNET

Some people prefer flip phones for their nostalgic designs and compact size. Motorola has plenty to choose from, but the best and most affordable pick for most people is the baseline 2026 Razr. 

The phone features a classic clamshell design and a spacious 3.6-inch cover screen, making it easy to check notifications, reply to texts, control music or follow navigation without opening the phone. The 6.9-inch inner display feels like using an average nonfolding phone, even if the screen is a little narrower and taller.

For most people, the Razr’s 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras and 32-megapixel selfie camera on the inner display will do the trick. There’s no room for a telephoto camera, but the Razr pulls its weight for more casual photography. 

The Motorola Razr 2026’s inner screen is 6.9 inches.David Lumb/CNET

The Razr’s processor isn’t as powerful as what you’ll get on the pricier Razr Plus and Razr Ultra, but as long as you’re not playing intensive games all day, you probably won’t notice the difference. 

The Razr’s $800 starting price is significantly lower than the cost of book-style folding devices like the iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8. The Razr could be a more appealing option for someone who doesn’t need a phone-tablet hybrid but just wants a phone that’s fun to use and taps into the nostalgia of the original Motorola Razr. 

No matter which phone you choose, your lucky recipient will enjoy the holiday spirit long after the season has passed, all while making quite the statement.

title: AirPods Pro 3 were worth the upgrade for one standout feature
snippet: AirPods Pro 3 (now only $149, down from $249) offer many advantages over AirPods Pro 2, but after a year of use, the improvements to Active Noise Cancellation alone have proven worth the upgrade. more…
fullText:
AirPods Pro 3 (now only $149, down from $249) offer many advantages over AirPods Pro 2, but after a year of use, the improvements to Active Noise Cancellation alone have proven worth the upgrade.

Apple doubled Active Noise Cancellation in AirPods Pro 3, and it’s been a huge upgrade

I’ve been using AirPods Pro 3 for over a year, and they had a lot to live up to because I already loved AirPods Pro 2 so much. Initially I found the new ear tips less comfortable, but thankfully that issue went away after a little extra time.

Some highlights of AirPods Pro 3 include the longer battery life, with 8 hours per charge compared to 6 on the previous model. The charging case’s new Ultra Wideband chip also makes it easier to find when it’s lost. Some users will appreciate the heart rate sensor, but I wear an Apple Watch all the time so it doesn’t benefit me much.

These new features are nice to have, but Active Noise Cancellation is where AirPods Pro 3 become a major upgrade. Apple says it’s “the world’s best in-ear Active Noise Cancellation.” Here’s how the new ANC compares to previous models:

removes up to 2x more noise than AirPods Pro 2

removes up to 4x more noise than AirPods Pro

I spend nearly my entire workday with AirPods Pro 3 in my ears. Whether I’m working from home with young kids around or at a busy coffee shop, I rely on ANC to block out background noise and help me focus.

One reason I’ve been especially impressed with the ANC upgrades is that I didn’t have any real complaints about ANC on AirPods Pro 2. But Apple managed to deliver improvements in AirPods Pro 3 I had no idea I needed, and when I’ve tried going back to AirPods Pro 2 I couldn’t believe how much noise was let in.

If Active Noise Cancellation is important to you, I highly recommend AirPods Pro 3.

snippet: The variety of gaming handhelds from Lenovo is about to get larger. Leaked details suggest the Lenovo Legion Go Beam will run Android instead of SteamOS on a high-refresh display. more…
fullText:
The variety of gaming handhelds from Lenovo is about to get larger. Leaked details suggest the Lenovo Legion Go Beam will run Android instead of SteamOS on a high-refresh display.

Lenovo is sticking with the Legion Go branding to offer something a little different to users. Instead of a SteamOS or Windows device, the Legion Go Beam is said to run Android (via Windows Latest). Specifically, Android 16.

That doesn’t limit it to Android titles alone. Android happens to make the perfect platform for cloud game streaming. Services like GeForce Now, Xbox Game Pass, and more offer a comparable experience to what a PC does for a fixed subscription, and that’s without the hardware internals something like the Legion Go 2 would need to run games natively.

The leak also notes the Lenovo Legion Go Beam will have a 7-inch 120Hz display, though there’s no information on what resolution or panel type the handheld might have. It’s likely 1080p or higher, though a lower resolution obviously will net users better performance. Battery is up in the air, too, other than a standard “long-lasting battery life” claim attributed to Lenovo.

	

This handheld takes a lot from the Legion Go 2 in design, as it should. It’s a comfortable device, and this shouldn’t be any different. It lacks a trackpad in favor of a traditional controller layout. It also has standard ports like one USB-C and 3.5mm headphone jack.

Pricing is a mystery. Devices like the Logitech G Cloud were such a hit because they delivered the needed performance at a good price. But those handhelds had a lower refresh rate. Still, hoping for a price tag around $350 or less isn’t such a bad thing.

title: Things 3.25 update brings new touch features to the MacBook Pro
snippet: Cultured Code is bringing swipe gestures to Things on Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro. Version 3.25 builds on the task manager’s basic touch support so you can schedule a to-do with a swipe or select several tasks with two fingers and drag them all at once. more…
fullText:
Cultured Code is bringing swipe gestures to Things on Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro. Version 3.25 builds on the task manager’s basic touch support so you can schedule a to-do with a swipe or select several tasks with two fingers and drag them all at once.

Swipe to schedule, select, and move to-dos

Say you’re going through your Today list and want to put something off until tomorrow. Swipe right on the to-do to open the date picker. Open it by touch and you’ll see taller rows that make dates easier to tap. Custom menus get the same treatment.

Swiping left selects a to-do. Swipe left again to deselect it. For a longer list, swipe up or down with two fingers to select several items at once. Then touch and hold any selected item to pick up the whole group, even if some of those tasks are offscreen. You can also drag individual to-dos and headings.

A single tap selects a to-do, and a second tap expands it. Double-tapping works too. Inside a to-do, checklist items are easier to reorder by touch. You can also cancel a to-do or checklist item by pressing and holding its checkbox.

Cultured Code has also made the sidebar easier to resize with a finger and given buttons throughout the Mac app larger tap targets.

The update follows Siri AI and Spotlight integration in Things 3.24 and more flexible scheduling for repeating to-dos in Things 3.23. You can find Things for Mac on the Mac App Store.

title: Motorola Razr (2027) reportedly gets big upgrades and an early January launch
snippet: According to a new report, Motorola’s next Razr flip phone is getting some major upgrades and a big schedule change, with Motorola Razr (2027) launching early next year. more…
fullText:
According to a new report, Motorola’s next Razr flip phone is getting some major upgrades and a big schedule change, with Motorola Razr (2027) launching early next year.

Android Headlines today published a new set of images of the Motorola Razr (2027), as well as key specs. The device is shown in three colors and apparently carries the codename “Raptor.” 

There are several key spec changes here, including:

Bigger 4-inch outer display,120Hz

144Hz inner 6.9-inch display

MediaTek Dimensity 7550X (MTK26M)

5,000 mAh battery (up from 4,800 mAh)

45W charging (up from 30W)

IPX8/IPX9, IP4X (up from IP48)

14.6mm thick (down from 15.85mm)

Motorola Razr (2027) is still only set for three Android OS updates and this new model is heavier at 195g (likely due to the bigger battery), but Motorola is very clearly making some big upgrades here. The biggest change is to the displays, both of which now match the Razr+ and Razr Ultra models. Some key specs, such as 8GB of RAM and 256GB of storage, are unchanged from the 2026 release. 

	

Motorola has been releasing its Razr series in the Spring, but today’s report claims that Razr (2027) will launch in January 2027, likely at CES and at the same time as the Razr Flex book-style foldable. There’s no word on new Plus or Ultra models yet.

fullText:
Welcome to Indie App Spotlight. This is a weekly 9to5Mac series where we showcase the latest apps in the indie app world. If you’re a developer and would like your app featured, get in contact.

You likely have a TV on your wall that generally sits idle throughout the day. While the Apple TV does offer loads of built in screensavers, you might be looking for something a bit more artsy. Salon offers a picture frame experience for the Apple TV, where it has over 1000 open-access paintings to display.

Highlights

In short, this app replicates the Samsung Frame TV experience but for anyone who owns an Apple TV. As mentioned above, you can choose from over 1000 hand-picked art pieces to choose from the world’s museums, but you can also import your own photos from iCloud.

Salon lets you add a frame to the edge of your photos, or you can display them edge-to-edge if you’d like. You can also add a clock and date to the corner.

The story

Here’s why the developer, Rene, decided to build Salon. If you’ve ever owned a Samsung Frame TV, you’ll likely resonate with the story:

I bought a Samsung Frame a few years back and was pretty appalled by Tizen and the fact that they charge a subscription for the art mode. It annoyed me enough to build my own, at first just for my own TV. I also noticed that tvOS gets very little love from indie developers. Outside Apple’s own apps and the big streaming apps, it’s mostly aquariums and fireplaces. Although now with the whole vibe coding craze, there are a few more interesting additions as well.

title: Not upgrading to iPhone 18 Pro or Duo? Here’s what’s coming in 2027
snippet: iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo have been out for quite some time now, and despite that, it’s still incredibly challenging to order an iPhone Duo in a timely manner. If for whatever reason you’re considering skipping out on this year’s iPhones, here’s what you have to look forward to next year. more…
fullText:
iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo have been out for quite some time now, and despite that, it’s still incredibly challenging to order an iPhone Duo in a timely manner. If for whatever reason you’re considering skipping out on this year’s iPhones, here’s what you have to look forward to next year.

2027 is going to be a relatively big iPhone release year for Apple. First, the company will be continuing the iPhone 18 lineup after it introduced a split release schedule. Then, in the fall, the company will debut a new round of flagships in celebration of the 20th anniversary of the iPhone. Here’s what to expect.

Spring 2027

iPhone 18

For the first time, Apple will be introducing its base iPhone in the spring. Upgrades for the iPhone 18 aren’t quite clear, though more RAM is one of the key rumors. Thermal upgrades will likely happen as well, as well as the new Apple C2 modem.

It’s possible Apple will update the design to fall more in line with the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro, though we don’t yet know.

This phone will of course equip the A20 chip, and it’ll probably start at the same $899 price point that iPhone 17 currently sits at – after it was increased from $799 in September.

iPhone 18e

This phone will most likely just end up being a chip bump from the A19 to A20 chip, and debut in the Spring alongside the iPhone 18. Earlier this year, reports indicated that Apple would share many components between the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e, though it isn’t quite clear what that could mean for the devices.

iPhone Air 2

Out of all of the spring iPhone releases, this one is the one to look forward to. After receiving a lukewarm reception with the initial iPhone Air model, Apple went back to the drawing board and decided to modify the design to fit an ultrawide camera into the device.

Personally, I don’t think an ultrawide camera is too important – though many people will see one camera on the back of the phone and immediately assume it’s less premium, so it’ll probably end up being an important upgrade for the sake of sales. Plus, ultrawide photos can be fun at times.

It should also have a larger battery, reportedly as large as 3500mAh. That’s a roughly 10% improvement from the original iPhone Air. iPhone Air 2 will likely also jump from Apples C1X modem to the C2.

Fall 2027

iPhone 20 Pro

For the 20th anniversary of the iPhone, Apple is expected to debut a fully redesigned iPhone to celebrate. It’ll reportedly be much more glassy, feature significantly slimmer bezels, a quad curved display, and ditch the flat edge design of the iPhone 12 and later. 

Personally, I’m slightly skeptical that this’ll truly be a replacement to the “Pro” phone for thermal reasons, but time will tell. iPhone Duo seemingly has strong thermals while not featuring an aluminum unibody, so my concern might not be relevant. It’ll offer two, larger display sizes: 6.4-inch and 7-inch. This largely comes from the bezel reduction.

	

If you’re holding out for iPhone 18 Pro, this “iPhone 20” is definitely the phone to wait out for.

iPhone Duo 2

Lastly, Apple will release a successor to its just-announced iPhone Duo next fall. Of course, you can expect next-generation Apple Silicon with the A21 Pro chip next year, but there aren’t many other substantial changes expected. Apple may bring proper Face ID to the outer display, an improvement from the recently-announced face unlock, but it’s unclear whether this feature will make the engineering cutoff date.

title: The Moto G Stylus (2025) at $200 is great only if a pen is a must
snippet: Okay, so here’s the deal (literally): last year’s Moto G Stylus (2025) is on sale right now on Amazon for just $199, and if you desperately need a digital writing tool with your phone, it’s a good buy. more…
fullText:
Okay, so here’s the deal (literally): last year’s Moto G Stylus (2025) is on sale right now on Amazon for just $199, and if you desperately need a digital writing tool with your phone, it’s a good buy.

That is the short answer; the long answer is a little more complicated, as due to some issues with the 2026 model, you are missing out on exactly…nothing. Yes, at under $200, you are getting essentially the same phone because Motorola decided that, due to RAM and storage shortages and price hikes, the newer model would forgo any major upgrades. The 2026 model starts at $499, so if you had your eye on it, yeah, it’s a silly way to waste $300 in our opinion.

It has the same Snapdragon 6 Gen 3 processor, 8GB RAM, and 128GB storage. There’s a 120Hz display too and the good news is you get a microSD card slot to expand the storage if you desperately need it. Other notable features include a 5,000mAh battery, 68W wired charging, 15W wireless charging, a 50MP camera setup, and, as of writing, it should be due for an Android 16 upgrade.

The star of the show of the Moto G Stylus (2025) is the stylus. It boils down to this: if you want a phone that isn’t a Galaxy Ultra, then this is the only other line that makes sense for document signers.

	

However, there are better deals out there. I think the Galaxy A56, at just $299, is an incredible offer right now and way more deserving of your hard-earned cash. Even so, if you want clean software or that stylus, the Moto G Stylus (2025) at $199 is at least an option especially for a family member or a backup to your existing phone.

title: CAD images suggest iPhone 18e will have an odd new camera design
snippet: CAD images of the iPhone 18e, said to come from a previously reliable source, have shown a rather odd new design for the camera bump. If accurate, it would represent a big change from its predecessor, which simply has a single lens protruding without a surrounding bump or plateau … more…
fullText:
CAD images of the iPhone 18e, said to come from a previously reliable source, have shown a rather odd new design for the camera bump.

If accurate, it would represent a big change from its predecessor, which simply has a single lens protruding without a surrounding bump or plateau …

The iPhone 17e was launched in March with a design unchanged from last year’s iPhone 16e. While the camera did get some feature enhancements, including the ability to store depth information for portrait photos, the physical camera design remained the same. 

The current model has a single lens protruding directly from the casing with a flush-mounted flashlight next to it. Engadget reports on CAD images showing a very different approach with next year’s iPhone 18e.

The renders show an almost square camera bump measuring about 28 mm by 35 mm that houses the single rear camera, the LED flash and the rear microphone.

The site doesn’t share the images, but says that the camera bump looks similar to that of the M5 iPad Pro, shown below.

It’s unclear what might have prompted the change of design, especially as the site’s Filipe Espósito says he’s also seen CAD models for the standard model iPhone 18 or the iPhone Air 2, neither of which adopt it.

Previous reports have suggested that the only spec change with the iPhone 18e over its predecessor will be performance improvements thanks to the A20 chip.
